newsitem.title: USA: Legato tumbles on downgrade after Q1 result.
newsitem.headline: Legato tumbles on downgrade after Q1 result.

text.p: Shares of Legato Systems dropped up to one third of their value on Thursday after a Wall Street firm dropped its rating on the thinly-covered stock, investors and analysts said.
In early afternoon, the company was trading down 4-5/8 at 12, after falling as low as 11 earlier in the session.
Oppenheimer and Co downgraded Legato Systems Inc to market perform from outperform, according to market sources.
Oppenheimer analyst Melissa Eisenstat was traveling and not immediately available for comment, her office said.
Legato executives were also not immediately available.
After the market close on Wednesday, Legato Systems Inc reported earnings per share for its first quarter rose to $0.17 a share, an 89 percent rise from operational earnings of $0.09 a year earlier.
The result was one penny, or 5.6 percent, below the $0.18 consensus of four analysts surveyed by First Call.

The computer network storage management software company cited strong growth of its product for Microsoft Corp's Windows NT platform, saying unit shipments of its NT server products for the first time exceeded Unix server shipments in the quarter.
Operating margin increased to 28 percent in the first quarter from 23 percent on an operational basis a year ago.

Robertson Stephens & Co analyst John Powers said the company's slight shortfall in earnings and revenue reflected the quick shift to NT from Unix among its customers, but added the company's strategy is addressing this movement. "They're in the midst of a really rapid shift from Unix to NT in terms of where the dominant revenue is coming from," he said. "I think underneath (the transitional issues) that is very positive news about the strength of the NT business," he said.
"We like the product flow and we like the mix shift once they get through this transition," he added.
Powers said he had retained a buy rating on the stock, and trimmed his full-year earnings per share estimate to $0.83 from $0.86, largely to reflect the first quarter shortfall.
Legato CEO Louis Cole had expressed confidence in a conference call with analysts that the company remains comfortable with Wall Street estimates for all of 1997.

Powers said Legato's strategy is to compete on the low end of the NT market with Novell Inc's NetWare products, but also provide added features at higher price points for companies moving from more feature-rich Unix systems.

"You've got to have a low entry point but the ability to capture revenue with additional features and add-ons and upgrades," he said. "As people go from Unix to NT, the initial revenue chunk they get from the initial sale is lower in the NT world. They make it up as they sell expanded capacity and more feature and function."

"As NT took off faster than expected, that left them with a steeper hill to climb this quarter in terms of the revenue from the initial sale," he said. "The good news is that they're putting a lot of seats out there that they can go in and sell higher NT follow-on business to."

Powers said he regards Legato as a franchise company in the market for backing up organizations' data from networks onto storage devices, with growth rates "close to or in excess of 50 percent year or year" although it is trading at less than 10 times the 1998 earnings estimate at Thursday's low.
Analysts' consensus estimate for 1998 was $1.19 a share before the first quarter results, according to Zacks.
"That's an unforgiving stock market. It's also a great buying opportunity," added Powers.
Other analysts said the company is still being challenged at the top end of its product line.

"Prices are coming down and the margins are skinnier," said UBS analyst Gibbs Moody, who said he dropped his rating to a neutral earlier this year, when the stock was trading around 28, due to the product transition.
((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau +415 846 5400))
